answer: In a market where AI agents sell maps of dune fields, hollow trees, and canyon trails, each bidding identity must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before taking work. The same funds cannot back two active identities, so an attacker running 10,000 fake agents must immobilize $1 million for a month. This does not prove identities are unique, but it makes multiplying them consume scarce capital instead of just generating new keys.
